findings.title: Public findMany() removed and replaced by getBaseConditions(), breaking existing callers
findings.body: The public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method is deleted. In its place is `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of rows. Any caller that does `service.findMany({ select, where, ... })` (for example the insights routers) will no longer compile. Those call sites would also need rewriting to use `$queryRaw`, and the PR does not update any of them. Either keep a compatibility path or update every consumer in the same PR.

findings.title: Authorization fragments are top-level ORs without outer parentheses
findings.body: For org and team scope, `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `(A) OR (B)` with no wrapping parentheses. A single eventTypeId filter likewise returns `(x) OR (y)` unwrapped. `getBaseConditions()` adds parentheses, but both getters are public. A consumer that writes `WHERE ${auth} AND "createdAt" > ...` or `WHERE ${filter} AND ${auth}` gets `A OR (B AND ...)` because of SQL operator precedence. That silently widens results and can bypass the authorization restriction. Return self-contained, parenthesized fragments, e.g. ``Prisma.sql`((${acc}) OR (${condition}))` ``.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `authConditions` is always a `Prisma.Sql` object and therefore always truthy, including NOTHING_CONDITION. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run. This misleadingly suggests the filter-only path could skip authorization. Simplify to: return auth alone when there is no filter, otherwise return auth AND filter.

findings.title: Constructor type weakened so invalid options compile and silently yield no data
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. Passing `scope: "team"` without `teamId` now type-checks. It then fails zod validation at runtime and silently becomes NOTHING_CONDITION (empty results) instead of being a compile-time error. The discriminated union type would catch this at compile time.

findings.title: Caching tests removed and authorization not verified end-to-end
findings.body: The caching tests for `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` were deleted rather than ported, so the caching behavior is now untested. The only test that runs SQL against the database uses user scope. The org and team scope fragments, which use `ANY()` array parameters and OR composition, are only compared structurally and never executed. Type or precedence errors in those fragments would therefore go unnoticed.
